# Fairstay Next Payer Planning (`fairstay-next-payer-planning`)

Plans the next payer for long-stay nursing-home residents: when Medicare Part A day 100 falls, when a managed care authorization ends, and when private funds run out, flagging residents with no next payer planned and private-pay residents who should start a Medicaid application now. Resident identifiers are masked before results reach the model.

**Fairstay Next Payer Planning never writes to residents or families.**

Fairstay ver 1 · Billing and revenue cycle · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · resident and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`fairstay-core`](../fairstay-core)

```bash
npx -y fairstay-next-payer-planning demo
npx -y fairstay-next-payer-planning mcp --root ./facility-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional Cedar Hollow residents, planned on 2026-03-10. Planted:

- R901: Part A since 1 January with 5 earlier days used, so day 100 falls on 5 April (26 days). No next payer is planned.
- R902: Part A since 5 January with 10 earlier days used, so day 100 falls on 4 April (25 days). Medicaid is planned.
- R903: a managed care authorization ends 20 March, with no plan.
- R904: private funds last about 64 days, with no Medicaid application.
- R905: funds last about 19 days, with Medicaid applied.
- R906 (Part A, early in the stay) and R907 (Medicaid) need nothing.

[`rules-typo.json`](fixtures/rules-typo.json) misspells a setting, so the check refuses it.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `nextpayer_check` | List residents whose current payer runs out soon, soonest first, and whether the next payer is planned. | runs |
| `nextpayer_write_report` | Write nextpayer-next-payer.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and nextpayer-next-payer.html into out_dir (default evergreen-out/nextpayer). | runs |
| `nextpayer_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `nextpayer_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `nextpayer_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `nextpayer_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `family_letter_send` | Fairstay Next Payer Planning never writes to residents or families. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `nextpayer_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `census` (required) | Census under --root: residents, payers and dates |
| `plans` (required) | Resident payer plans under --root: next payer, Part A days used earlier, managed care authorization end, private funds, daily rate, monthly income, Medicaid application date |
| `rules` | Optional rules JSON: horizon_days, apply_lead_days |
| `as_of` | Date to plan from (YYYY-MM-DD, default today) |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold resident or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx fairstay-next-payer-planning inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Census (`census`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `resident_id` | text (masked) | Resident ID, Resident #, Resident Number, Res ID, Res #, MRN, Medical Record Number, Client ID |
| `resident_name` | text (masked) | Resident, Resident Name, Name, Patient, Patient Name, Client Name, Resident Full Name |
| `facility` | text | Facility, Facility Name, Building, Location, Fac, Center |
| `from` (required) | date | From, Start, Start Date, Effective Date, Begin Date, From Date, Admit Date, Census Date |
| `to` | date | To, End, End Date, Thru, Through, Thru Date, Through Date, To Date |
| `payer` (required) | text | Payer, Payer Name, Primary Payer, Pay Source, Payer Source, Payor, Payor Name, Insurance |
| `payer_type` | text | Payer Type, Payor Type, Payer Class, Payer Category, Pay Type |
| `level` | text | Level, Level of Care, Care Level, Rate Type, Rate Level, Room Type, Accommodation, RUG |
| `bed_status` | text | Bed Status, Status, Census Status, Action, Census Action, Leave Type |
| `room` | text | Room, Room Bed, Bed, Room/Bed, Unit |

### Payer plans (`plans`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `resident_id` | text (masked) | Resident ID, Resident #, Resident Number, Res ID, Res #, MRN, Medical Record Number, Client ID |
| `resident_name` | text (masked) | Resident, Resident Name, Name, Patient, Patient Name, Client Name, Resident Full Name |
| `next_payer` | text | Next Payer, Planned Payer, Future Payer, Payer Plan |
| `part_a_days_used` | number | Part A Days Used, Prior SNF Days, Benefit Days Used |
| `auth_end` | date | Auth End, Authorization End, Auth Through, Auth Expires |
| `private_funds` | amount | Private Funds, Funds Available, Assets, Bank Balance |
| `daily_rate` | amount | Daily Rate, Private Rate, Per Diem |
| `monthly_income` | amount | Monthly Income, Income, Social Security, Pension |
| `medicaid_applied_on` | date | Medicaid Applied, Medicaid Applied On, Application Date |

## Settings file (`nextpayer_rules`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `horizon_days` | Look this many days ahead (default 30) |
| `apply_lead_days` | Flag private-pay residents this many days before funds run out with no Medicaid application (default 90) |

## Memory

`nextpayer_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `nextpayer_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|
| `planning_note` | is shown with results. It never changes a check. |

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `fairstay-core` and `fairclaim-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fairstay-next-payer-planning": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "fairstay-next-payer-planning",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/facility-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add fairstay-next-payer-planning -- npx -y fairstay-next-payer-planning mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
fairstay-next-payer-planning tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
fairstay-next-payer-planning sources               # the columns each input is read from
fairstay-next-payer-planning inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
fairstay-next-payer-planning call nextpayer_check '{"census":"<census>","plans":"<plans>"}'
fairstay-next-payer-planning eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
fairstay-next-payer-planning demo
```

## Resident and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: resident and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to PointClickCare, MatrixCare, a payer portal, a bank, a state Medicaid portal or a payroll system.
- Medicare, Medicaid and payroll rules are summarised from public material as of 2026 and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, payroll or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, tax, accounting, clinical, reimbursement or HIPAA advice. A person decides what to bill, pay, appeal, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
